recommendation: Keep the core audit commit as-is. Revisit FHIR-40717 with TI/Vocab before changing source; likely follow-up belongs in the Extension Pack valueset-toocostly status/description and in core ValueSet/$expand incomplete-expansion guidance, coordinated with FHIR-42811 and FHIR-49701 once those later decisions are Applied or Published.
issue_request: FHIR-40717 was an Applied/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core ValueSet tracker requesting better documentation of http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/valueset-toocostly. The approved resolution said to deprecate valueset-too-costly, add structuredefinition-standards-status=deprecated, and add text to the definition and description saying it was used in STU3 and earlier terminology services and that newer terminology servers should communicate the information with OperationOutcome issue code too-costly.
initial_application: No current FHIR-core StructureDefinition source exists for valueset-toocostly because core extension definitions moved to the FHIR Extension Pack. Extension Pack commit 2d8d6741385fe7229cd5fbeb5ee276ec0abe31a5 applied FHIR-40717 by adding the deprecated standards-status extension and the approved STU3/OperationOutcome too-costly wording; 5d9a90e4e3a86095519075d326a1109b9a3f2e30 removed the duplicate trial-use status; ea2d7b0ee5b77e9fe38e889cfc778d87e4edf776 later changed the artifact status to retired.
additional_context: Current core ValueSet/$expand documentation already says overly large expansions may return OperationOutcome code too-costly, and OperationOutcome.issue.code defines too-costly. July 2025 TI minutes for FHIR-40717 say the prior response may have missed the distinction between a too-costly operation error and marking an incomplete response with too-costly as the reason. Later related FHIR-core issues FHIR-49701 and FHIR-42811 continue the incomplete/unclosed/too-costly expansion discussion but are only Resolved - change required in this default run.
reconciliation: No FHIR-core source change was made. The reconciliation published an empty human-review audit commit because the authoritative extension definition is external to this checkout, the original Extension Pack application already reflects the 2024 resolution, and later 2025-2026 evidence shows the remaining semantics need work-group review before automated source changes are safe.
